title: Israel Enslaved in Egypt
summary: A new king who does not remember Joseph fears Israel's rapid growth and forces the people into hard labor. When Hebrew midwives refuse to kill newborn boys, Pharaoh orders every infant son thrown into the Nile.
blurb: Pharaoh enslaves Israel and orders infant sons drowned

title: Moses Born and Flees
summary: A Hebrew baby is hidden, set afloat on the Nile, and rescued by Pharaoh's daughter, who raises him as her own. Grown, Moses kills an Egyptian and flees to Midian, where he marries Zipporah. Egypt's king dies, and God hears Israel's groaning.
blurb: Baby Moses is rescued from the Nile, then flees to Midian

title: The Burning Bush
summary: While tending sheep near Horeb, Moses sees a bush ablaze yet unburned and God speaks to him from within it. God sends Moses to rescue Israel from slavery and, when Moses asks, reveals his covenant name.
blurb: God calls Moses from a burning bush at Horeb

title: Moses Sent Back to Egypt
summary: God equips Moses with miraculous signs and answers his objections about speaking ability by appointing Aaron as his mouthpiece. Moses leaves Midian, reunites with Aaron, and together they convince Israel's elders to believe.
blurb: Moses returns to Egypt with Aaron as his spokesman

title: Pharaoh Refuses and Retaliates
summary: Moses and Aaron ask Pharaoh to let Israel go worship in the wilderness, but he refuses and accuses them of laziness. Pharaoh punishes the request by making the Israelites gather their own straw for bricks.
blurb: Pharaoh refuses Moses and forces Israel to gather their own straw

title: God Renews His Promise
summary: Discouraged by Pharaoh's cruelty, Moses hears God reaffirm his covenant name and his promise to redeem Israel and bring the people into the promised land. God sends Moses and Aaron back to confront Pharaoh again.
blurb: God reaffirms his covenant name and promise to Moses

title: The Nile Turns to Blood
summary: Aaron's staff becomes a snake and swallows the Egyptian magicians' staffs, but Pharaoh's heart remains hard. Aaron then strikes the Nile with his staff, turning the entire river to blood and killing its fish.
blurb: Aaron's staff becomes a snake; the Nile turns to blood

title: Frogs, Gnats, and Flies
summary: Three plagues strike in succession: frogs overrun Egypt until Pharaoh briefly relents, dust turns to gnats that even the magicians cannot reproduce, and swarms of flies fill Egyptian homes while sparing Israel's land of Goshen.
blurb: Plagues of frogs, gnats, and flies strike Egypt

title: Livestock, Boils, and Hail
summary: A plague kills Egypt's livestock while Israel's animals are spared, painful boils break out on the Egyptians, and a violent hailstorm mixed with fire destroys crops and anything left exposed across the land.
blurb: Plagues of dead livestock, boils, and hail strike Egypt

title: Locusts and Darkness
summary: A locust swarm devours every plant the hail left standing, stripping Egypt bare. Then a thick, unnatural darkness covers the land for three days while Israel's homes remain lit, and still Pharaoh refuses to yield.
blurb: Locusts strip Egypt bare, then darkness covers the land

title: Warning of the Final Plague
summary: God tells Moses one more plague remains: the death of every firstborn in Egypt. This time Pharaoh himself will beg Israel to leave, and Moses warns Pharaoh directly before the plague falls that night.
blurb: Moses warns Pharaoh of the coming death of the firstborn

title: The Passover and the Exodus
summary: God institutes the Passover meal and the protective blood on Israel's doorframes. The tenth plague kills every Egyptian firstborn, Pharaoh finally releases Israel, and the people leave Rameses after four hundred thirty years in Egypt.
blurb: The Passover instituted; Israel finally leaves Egypt

title: Consecration and the Pillar
summary: God commands that every firstborn male among Israel's people and animals be set apart to him as a lasting reminder of the exodus. God then leads the people by a visible pillar of cloud and fire.
blurb: Israel's firstborn consecrated; God leads by cloud and fire

title: Crossing the Red Sea
summary: Pharaoh changes his mind and pursues Israel, trapping the people against the sea. The LORD parts the water so Israel crosses on dry ground, then closes the sea again and drowns the pursuing Egyptian army.
blurb: Israel crosses the parted Red Sea; Egypt's army drowns

title: The Song of the Sea
summary: After crossing the sea, Moses and Israel sing praise to the LORD and Miriam leads the women in dance. Three days later the people find bitter water at Marah, and the LORD sweetens it, then leads them to the springs of Elim.
blurb: Israel sings after the sea, then finds bitter water

title: Manna and Quail in the Wilderness
summary: Israel grumbles for food in the wilderness of Sin, and the LORD provides quail each evening and bread called manna each morning, with instructions to gather double on the sixth day and rest on the seventh.
blurb: The LORD provides manna, quail, and a Sabbath pattern

title: Water from the Rock and Victory over Amalek
summary: Israel quarrels with Moses over water at Rephidim, and the LORD provides water from the rock at Horeb. Amalek then attacks, and Israel prevails as long as Moses' hands, held up by Aaron and Hur, stay lifted.
blurb: Moses strikes the rock; Israel defeats Amalek

title: Jethro's Advice to Moses
summary: Jethro brings Moses' wife and sons to him in the wilderness and rejoices at what the LORD has done for Israel. Seeing Moses judge the people alone all day, Jethro advises him to appoint capable men over smaller groups.
blurb: Jethro advises Moses to share the burden of judging

title: Israel Arrives at Sinai
summary: Israel camps before Mount Sinai, and the LORD proposes a covenant, calling the people to be his treasured possession and a kingdom of priests. The people consecrate themselves for three days, and the LORD descends on the mountain in thunder, fire, and smoke.
blurb: The LORD descends on Sinai in fire and thunder

title: The Ten Commandments
summary: God speaks the Ten Commandments directly to Israel from the mountain. Terrified by the thunder, lightning, and trumpet blast, the people beg Moses to speak for God instead, and God gives instructions about building altars.
blurb: God speaks the Ten Commandments to a terrified Israel

title: Laws on Servants and Injuries
summary: The LORD gives Moses case laws covering Hebrew servants, violence between people, and compensation for injury or loss, including the principle of eye for eye and tooth for tooth as a limit on retaliation.
blurb: Laws on servants, injury, and eye for eye

title: Laws on Property and the Vulnerable
summary: The LORD gives laws on restitution for theft and property damage, protection for widows, orphans, and sojourners, lending without charging interest to the poor, and offering the firstfruits and firstborn to him.
blurb: Laws protecting property, the poor, and lending fairly

title: Justice, the Feasts, and the Promised Angel
summary: The LORD commands impartial justice, rest for the land every seventh year, and three annual feasts to be kept before him. He promises to send his angel ahead of Israel and warns against worshiping the gods of Canaan.
blurb: God promises to send his angel before Israel

title: The Covenant Ratified with Blood
summary: Israel agrees to all the LORD's words, and Moses sprinkles the blood of the covenant on the people. Moses, Aaron, and seventy elders go up and see the God of Israel, and Moses then enters the cloud on the mountain for forty days and nights.
blurb: Moses sprinkles the blood of the covenant

title: Instructions for the Ark, Table, and Lampstand
summary: The LORD calls for a freewill offering of materials and gives Moses detailed instructions for building the ark of the covenant with its mercy seat, the table for the bread of the Presence, and the golden lampstand.
blurb: Plans for the ark of the covenant

title: Instructions for the Tabernacle Structure
summary: The LORD gives detailed instructions for the tabernacle's linen curtains, wooden frames, and coverings, and for the veil that will separate the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place where the ark will rest.
blurb: Plans for the tabernacle's curtains and frame

title: Instructions for the Bronze Altar and Courtyard
summary: The LORD gives instructions for the bronze altar of burnt offering and for the courtyard that will surround the tabernacle, with its linen hangings, and commands Israel to keep oil burning in the lamp continually.
blurb: Plans for the bronze altar and courtyard

title: Instructions for the Priestly Garments
summary: The LORD gives instructions for the sacred garments Aaron and his sons will wear as priests, including the ephod and the breastpiece of judgment set with twelve stones representing Israel's tribes, and the Urim and Thummim.
blurb: Plans for Aaron's ephod and breastpiece

title: Instructions for Ordaining the Priests
summary: The LORD gives detailed instructions for the seven-day ceremony that will ordain Aaron and his sons as priests, including specific sacrifices, anointing with oil, and the daily burnt offering to be kept at the tabernacle's entrance.
blurb: Plans for ordaining Aaron and his sons

title: Instructions for the Incense Altar and Basin
summary: The LORD gives instructions for the altar of incense, the atonement money collected in a census, the bronze basin for washing, and the recipes for the anointing oil and incense that are reserved for sacred use alone.
blurb: Plans for the incense altar and basin

title: Bezalel, Oholiab, and the Tablets of the Testimony
summary: The LORD appoints craftsmen filled with his Spirit to build the tabernacle and everything in it, reaffirms the Sabbath as a lasting sign of the covenant, and gives Moses the two stone tablets written by his own finger.
blurb: God gives Moses the two stone tablets

title: The Golden Calf
summary: While Moses delays on the mountain, the people persuade Aaron to make a golden calf to worship. God threatens to destroy Israel, but Moses intercedes. Coming down, Moses breaks the tablets, destroys the calf, and the Levites execute judgment on the guilty.
blurb: Israel worships a golden calf while Moses is away

title: Moses Seeks the LORD's Presence
summary: The LORD says he will not personally go with the stiff-necked people, and Israel mourns. Moses meets with the LORD face to face at the tent of meeting, pleads for his presence to go with them, and asks to see his glory.
blurb: Moses asks the LORD to show him his glory

title: The Covenant Renewed and Moses' Shining Face
summary: Moses cuts new tablets, and the LORD passes before him proclaiming his name as merciful, gracious, and slow to anger. The LORD renews the covenant, and Moses comes down with a face shining so brightly he must wear a veil.
blurb: The LORD proclaims his name; Moses' face shines

title: Israel's Offering for the Tabernacle
summary: Moses gathers Israel, restates the Sabbath command, and calls for a freewill offering of materials to build the tabernacle. Men and women whose hearts are stirred bring gold, silver, bronze, yarns, wood, and gems generously.
blurb: Israel brings materials to build the tabernacle

title: More Than Enough Is Given
summary: The people bring so much material for the tabernacle that Moses has to restrain them from giving any more. Bezalel and the craftsmen begin constructing the tabernacle's curtains, frames, and coverings exactly as the LORD commanded.
blurb: The people give more than enough for the work

title: The Ark, Table, and Lampstand Are Built
summary: Bezalel builds the ark of the covenant with its mercy seat and cherubim, the table for the bread of the Presence, the golden lampstand, and the altar of incense, following the pattern the LORD gave Moses.
blurb: The ark and lampstand are built as instructed

title: The Bronze Altar and Courtyard Are Built
summary: The craftsmen build the bronze altar and the tabernacle's courtyard with its hangings and posts, and the text records the exact amounts of gold, silver, and bronze that Israel contributed to the whole project.
blurb: The bronze altar is built; materials are recorded

title: The Priestly Garments Finished and Moses' Blessing
summary: The craftsmen finish Aaron's priestly garments exactly as the LORD commanded, down to the engraved gold plate reading "Holy to the LORD." Moses inspects all the completed work and blesses the people for their labor.
blurb: Moses inspects the finished work and blesses Israel

title: The Tabernacle Set Up and Filled with Glory
summary: Moses sets up the tabernacle and its furnishings exactly as commanded, and the glory of the LORD fills it so completely that even Moses cannot enter. From then on, the cloud of the LORD guides when Israel sets out and when it stays.
blurb: The glory of the LORD fills the tabernacle
